campaign.name: gpt-oss-20b-dataset-v1-dgx
campaign.description: DGX Spark (GB10 Grace Blackwell, ARM64) llama.cpp vs vLLM A/B; shares the RTX 4090 matrix, seed, durations and stability limits so both backends stay comparable across hardware
campaign._gpu_idle_utilization_pct_note: RTX 4090 reference used 5. Raised to 12 on DGX Spark: this host runs a graphical desktop (gnome-remote-desktop-daemon holds the GPU) and an idle vLLM EngineCore still polls, so measured idle utilisation floors at 7-8% and the strict '< threshold' test at line 160 of run_benchmarks.py could never pass. Working utilisation is 94%, so 12 still separates busy from idle. This gates when a run may start; it does not affect what is measured.

llama-cpp.deployment: GPT-OSS-20B MXFP4 GGUF on DGX Spark GB10, context=65536, parallel=16; llama.cpp b8407 aarch64 CUDA build recorded in llama_server.build

vllm.deployment: vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:928dde7d6c19478c9c6ab975fed12e6466f6d9b7cb3695d218e287c0c88ad608 (linux/arm64, tag nightly pulled 2026-08-07, vLLM 0.26.1rc1.dev457+gc810e5ee9, build commit c810e5ee9976ad86b81d1277b53e76d0ee639414); GPT-OSS-20B HF revision 6cee5e81, quantization gpt_oss_mxfp4 via MARLIN MoE backend, TRITON_ATTN; max-model-len=65536, max-num-seqs=16; gpu-memory-utilization=0.70 on 121.7 GiB unified memory, measured KV pool 68.01 GiB / 2790787 tokens (max concurrency 42.58x at 65536) so this host never preempts at the comparison matrix's concurrency<=16, unlike the 24 GB RTX 4090; harmony tokenizer needs o200k_base.tiktoken mounted at TIKTOKEN_ENCODINGS_BASE or chat completions fail with HTTP 500; client load up to concurrency=64
vllm._url_note: Host port. The RTX 4090 campaign published the container's 8000 on host 18000; keep that mapping or change this URL to match whatever the DGX container publishes.
vllm._memory_note: --gpu-memory-utilization is a fraction of the memory vLLM sees. On GB10 that pool is unified LPDDR5X shared with the host, so the same 0.90 that was safe on a 24 GB discrete 4090 reserves a far larger absolute amount here and starves the OS. Choose it deliberately and record the value in the report.

vllm-120b._cell_backend_note: Cells are tagged with the backend family ('vllm'), not the deployment name. This key lets a second vLLM deployment select the same matrix without duplicating 79 cells. Results still land in results/vllm-120b/ because the run directory uses the deployment name.
vllm-120b._tokenizer_note: tokenizer.json, tokenizer_config.json, special_tokens_map.json and chat_template.jinja are byte-identical between the 20B and 120B snapshots (verified 2026-08-18 by sha256). The prepared datasets were bucket-sliced with the 20B tokenizer and are therefore valid here without regeneration; this path points at the 120B snapshot for provenance only.
vllm-120b.deployment: vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:928dde7d6c19478c9c6ab975fed12e6466f6d9b7cb3695d218e287c0c88ad608 (same image as the 20B campaign); GPT-OSS-120B HF revision b5c939de, quantization mxfp4 via MARLIN MoE backend, TRITON_ATTN; max-model-len=65536, max-num-seqs set per campaign via start_vllm_120b.sh; gpu-memory-utilization=0.85 measured 33.07-35.25 GiB KV pool / 904670-964375 tokens across two identical launches, so the pool varies ~6% run to run because the unified memory is shared with a graphical desktop -- pin it with --kv-cache-memory before the formal campaign. The reported 'maximum concurrency 13.80x' is 904670/65536 and only binds on full-length requests; the whole 79-cell matrix fits, the heaviest cell being rag-*-b016k-c32 at ~532K tokens. Weights+non-torch 66.68 GiB, cold load ~9.7 min.
vllm-120b._url_note: start_vllm_120b.sh publishes the container's 8000 on host 18001 so it cannot be confused with the 20B deployment on 18000. The DFlash variant uses 18002.

llama_server._comment: Flags were hardcoded in the RTX 4090 harness. They are config-driven here so the aarch64 CUDA build's actual capabilities can be probed and the values used end up in the run manifest. Run probe_llama_server.sh first.
llama_server.build: b8407 (312cf0332) aarch64 CUDA sm_121, GNU 13.3.0, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.142; probe 2026-08-16: flash-attn on / kv-unified / cache-prompt all OK, ctx=65536 parallel=16 boot ok
llama_server._build_values: Record what the aarch64 CUDA build reports, e.g. 'b8407 aarch64 CUDA sm_121'. Confirm the arch with: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=compute_cap --format=csv,noheader
llama_server._flash_attn_values: on | off | auto | unset (unset omits the flag entirely). The RTX 4090 campaign used 'on'; keep it unless the probe shows the aarch64 build rejects it.
